paper.title: Minimax-Optimal Online Contract Design with Unrestricted Bounded Contracts

settings.name_in_paper: Online contract design with unrestricted bounded contracts and outcome-category feedback
unmapped: Principal-agent contract design: actions are payment vectors f in [0,1]^m over m outcomes; agent of random type best-responds with a fixed (history-independent) selection rule; principal utility u(f)=P(f).(v-f) may be discontinuous in f
Feedback is the realized outcome category (one-hot vector over m outcomes), which is stronger than scalar bandit reward feedback; hidden actions/types are not observed
Stackelberg regret against the best fixed contract
Learner knows number of outcomes m and value vector v
settings.definition_quote: After posting $f$ given history $\mathcal H$, the principal observes the realized outcome as a one-hot vector $X$ satisfying $\mathbb E[X\mid f,\mathcal H]=P(f)$. ... The principal's expected one-period utility is $u(f)=P(f)\cdot(v-f)$. ... $\mathfrak R_T=T\sup_{f\in[0,1]^m}u(f)-\mathbb E[\sum_{t=1}^T u(f_t)]$.

symbols.C_m: constant depending only on number of outcomes m

conditions: selected best responses fixed independently of learner history (Assumption 1)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For every fixed $m\ge2$, there exists a finite constant $B_m$, depending only on $m$, such that, for every $T\ge2$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, Algorithms~\ref{alg:simulator}-\ref{alg:master} with confidence $\delta=T^{-2}$ use only $m$, $v$, $T$, and $\varepsilon$ and satisfy, on every instance in $\mathcal I_m$, \[ \mathfrak R_T\le C_m\big(T\varepsilon+L_T\sqrt{TK_\varepsilon}+K_\varepsilon\big),\]

results.notes: Regret is Stackelberg regret defined via expected utilities (pseudo-regret). Compute polynomial in T for fixed m but exponential in m.

symbols.m_out: total number of outcomes (fixed); hidden constant depends on m_out

conditions: selected best responses fixed independently of learner history (Assumption 1)
tuning: eps_alg ~ T^{-1/(m_out+1)} up to log factors

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Consequently, $\varepsilon\asymp T^{-1/(m+1)}$ up to logarithmic factors gives $\mathfrak R_T\le\widetilde O_m(T^{m/(m+1)})$.

symbols.c_m: positive constant depending only on m_out

conditions: hard instances: single type, finite action set, value vector (1,...,1,0), nonnegative costs bounded by one, common deterministic action-priority tie-breaking

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: For every fixed $m\ge2$, there is $c_m>0$ such that every adaptive outcome-feedback policy and every $T\ge1$ incur $\mathfrak R_T\ge c_mT^{m/(m+1)}$ on some finite-action, single-type instance in $\mathcal I_m$.

results.notes: Holds for outcome-category feedback, hence also for weaker scalar feedback. Stated as explicit c_m T^{m/(m+1)}; recorded as Omega.

cited_results.setting_description: Online contract design with unrestricted bounded contracts, m outcomes, outcome feedback
